findings.summary: cross-component-contract: the helper waits for a re-hand-over the bridge never makes when an acknowledgement is refused for its lease on a settled item
findings.recommendation: Scope: class. `bridgeStore.outbound.ackVerdict` (lib/bridge-store.js) judges the lease before the item's own state: a lease row that is gone answers `lease-not-found`, one issued to another token answers `lease-not-yours`, and only after both does a delivered item answer `already-delivered` or a dropped one `expired`. `acknowledge` in lib/bridge-helper/outbound.js treats `LEASE_NOT_FOUND` and `LEASE_NOT_YOURS` (with `LEASE_LAPSED`) as 'the bridge hands it over again and it is acknowledged then', keeps the entry as `posted`, and retries it at the top of every pass with the stored `leaseId`. For an item the bridge has already settled that hand-over never comes, so the entry is retried forever. Two reachable ways in, both read from the code: (1) the helper token is replaced while the helper holds a posted, unacknowledged item, and the item is then let go by retention (non-reply kinds) or was in fact delivered by an acknowledgement whose answer was lost: every later attempt answers 403 `LEASE_NOT_YOURS`, never 410 or 200; (2) the helper is away for more than `RETENTION.settledLeaseMs` (24 h) after such a lost answer or lapse, the lease row is pruned while the item row stays for 30 days, and the answer is 404 `LEASE_NOT_FOUND`. Nothing is posted twice and nothing is lost, but the entry never leaves `state.json`, the helper makes one doomed request and logs `outbound-ack-failed` on every pass for good, and docs/operator-bridge-helper.md tells the operator that code means 'It is acknowledged on a later pass'. `settle` cannot clear it (it takes held items only). The existing tests cover the same-token cases only ('lets go of its record when the bridge has let the item go', 'drops a claim in progress when the helper token was replaced' where the item is still waiting). Close it on one side of the contract rather than per code: either have the bridge answer for a settled item's state in a way the helper can tell is final (for example a terminal code when the item is delivered or dropped and the presented lease cannot be honoured), or have the helper stop retrying a `posted` entry that the bridge neither accepts nor hands over again within a bound, and say so with a closed code. Add a test for token replacement followed by expiry, and one for a pruned lease. The same missing terminal path applies to a `posting` entry (parts sent, or `since` set) whose item is dropped at the bridge: it is never claimed again, so it is never revisited or removed; bound that too.

findings.summary: The one-helper lock trusts a bare pid, so a reused pid keeps the helper from starting and `status` reports it as running

After an exit that did not run `lock.release()` (power loss, SIGKILL, launchd's kill when a pass outlasts its exit timeout) the file keeps the old pid, and after a reboot that number commonly belongs to some other process. The helper then logs `helper-already-running` with that pid and exits 78, launchd restarts it every 30 seconds with the same result, nothing is relayed in either direction, and `tc-bridge-helper status` prints `helper: running (pid N)` because it applies the same test. The test 'takes over a lock a dead helper left' covers a dead pid only. Make the lock prove more than liveness: record alongside the pid something a stranger's process cannot match (the process start time, or check that the pid's command is this helper) and treat a mismatch as a lock left behind; have `status` use the same judgement; cover a live-but-foreign pid in the test.

findings.summary: The helper process outlives its own stop by up to the poll or backoff delay
findings.recommendation: Scope: instance. In `run` (lib/bridge-helper/cli.js) a stop resolves the `wake` side of `Promise.race([sleep(delay), ...])`, but the default `sleep` is a plain `setTimeout` that is neither cleared nor unref'd, and bin/tc-bridge-helper replaces the default SIGTERM/SIGINT behaviour with `process.once` and sets only `process.exitCode`. After `helper-stop` is logged and the lock released, the process therefore stays alive until that timer fires: up to `pollSeconds` (15 s by default, 300 s at most) or the 5-minute backoff ceiling. Inbound's retry sleeps do the same on a smaller scale. No message is lost or repeated and the lock is already free, so nobody acts wrongly on it; under launchd the job is killed at its exit timeout, and at a terminal a second Ctrl-C ends it. The end-to-end test injects its own `sleep`, so it cannot see this. If it is worth a line: clear or unref the pending timer on stop, or exit explicitly from the launcher once `main` resolves.

findings.summary: Helper posts a part it never recorded: an attempt marker that failed to save is kept in memory and treated as recorded on the next pass
findings.recommendation: Scope: instance (lib/bridge-helper/outbound.js, relay() + save()). Why it broke: `entry.since` carries two meanings, 'an attempt is durably on record' and 'an attempt began', and the in-memory `unsaved` map is a second source of truth beside state.json that keeps the first meaning alive after the write that would have made it true has failed. Conditions observed: (1) pass N: noteClaim(nonce) writes fine; relay() sets `entry.since = now()` and calls save(); state.set throws; save() stores that entry, `since` included, in `unsaved` and throws Reported. No post was made, which is correct. (2) pass N+1: state.claim() still names the claim, ask() returns the same live lease, relay() reads the entry through entryOf() from `unsaved`; `opened = !entry.since` is false, so the pre-post save() is skipped and rest.createMessage() runs with no write attempted first. The post is made with nothing on disk saying an attempt began. If the helper then dies before the post-success save lands (or that save fails too and the process is restarted), the restart finds no entry and posts the item again; only Discord's nonce window stands between that and a duplicate, which is exactly the case the `since`/`uncertain` path exists to catch. This also makes three shipped statements false: docs/operator-bridge-helper.md ('The record cannot be written: The helper posts nothing it could not record first'), log.js's `state-write-failed` meaning, and state.js's header ('a caller that could not record an attempt has not made one'). test/bridge-helper-relay.test.js:562 covers only the first failing pass, and there the failure is taken by noteClaim before relay() is reached, so the path is untested. Fix in the code, not the prose: when the pre-post save fails, do not keep `since` on the entry held in `unsaved` (delete it before stashing, or do not stash an entry whose only change is `since`), so the next pass sees `opened === true` and must record before posting. Add a test in which the claim write succeeds, the pre-post write fails once, and the following pass must write before any post reaches the stand-in Discord.

findings.summary: A posted item whose lease row has been pruned is retried every pass for up to 30 days: the helper reads LEASE_NOT_FOUND as 'will be handed over again', the bridge answers it before looking at the item's terminal state
findings.recommendation: Scope: instance, two ends of one contract (lib/bridge-store.js outbound.ackVerdict order; lib/bridge-helper/outbound.js acknowledge()). Why it broke: ackVerdict checks 'lease-not-found' and 'lease-not-yours' before the item's own state, and settled leases are pruned 24 hours after settling while a delivered or dropped item stays for 30 days, so for 29 days the item's terminal state is unreachable to an acknowledgement. Conditions: helper entry `posted` with a leaseId; at the bridge the item is `delivered` (the ack was applied and its answer lost) or `dropped` (a notification past its limit, e.g. fleet-idle at 24 hours); the lease row is gone. The helper's first loop in pass() acknowledges under entry.leaseId, gets 404 LEASE_NOT_FOUND, logs `outbound-ack-failed`, returns false and keeps the entry, on the stated ground that 'the bridge hands it over again and it is acknowledged then'. A delivered or dropped item is never handed over again, so the same call and the same log line repeat every poll (15 s by default) until retention removes the item and the answer becomes OUTBOUND_NOT_FOUND. Who does what wrong: the operator reading the log sees `outbound-ack-failed` indefinitely, and docs/operator-bridge-helper.md tells them it 'is acknowledged on a later pass'; the entry is not `held`, so `status` shows nothing to settle. It needs the helper to be unable to acknowledge for over 24 hours after a post (stopped mid-flight, or holding a replaced token), so it is rare, but nothing ends it. It also leaves two shipped statements untrue: ackVerdict's own comment ('An item already delivered answers the same way however old its lease is') and docs/operator-bridge.md ('refused with 410 OUTBOUND_EXPIRED, every time, whatever lease it names'). Remedy, one of: (a) in ackVerdict judge the item's terminal state before the lease lookup where that is safe to disclose to a verified helper token (dropped -> expired; delivered with the same reference -> already-delivered), which makes both statements true and lets the helper forget; or (b) keep settled leases as long as their item. Either way add a relay test that prunes the lease between post and acknowledgement.

findings.summary: The one-helper lock's stale-owner takeover is check-then-act
findings.recommendation: Scope: instance (lib/bridge-helper/cli.js takeLock()). Why: when the lock file names a dead pid, the taker removes the file and loops to create it again; two processes that both read the same dead owner (launchd's `run` and an operator's `settle` or a second `run` started together after a crash) can each remove and re-create, the second removing the first's fresh lock, and both then believe they hold it. The module's own stated reason for the lock is that two helpers post every item twice. The window is a few file-system calls wide and needs a stale lock plus two simultaneous starts, so NOTE. If closed: take over by an atomic step that only one contender can win, e.g. write the new pid to a temp file and `link`/`rename` it over the stale file only after re-reading that it still names the same dead pid, or hold an exclusive lock on a file that is never removed.

findings.summary: A lock left by an unclean stop can make the helper refuse to start while `status` reports it running
findings.recommendation: Scope: instance. `cli.js#takeLock` decides a lock is live from `process.kill(pid, 0)` alone (EPERM counts as alive), and `status` uses the same test on the same file. The lock is released only on the SIGTERM/SIGINT path at the end of `run`; a SIGKILL, a crash or a power loss leaves `helper.pid` behind. After a reboot the recorded pid is very likely to belong to some other process (a login-time LaunchAgent gets a low pid, and those are densely reused), so every launchd restart logs `helper-already-running` and exits 78 forever, while `tc-bridge-helper status` prints `helper: running (pid N)` and then the previous run's snapshot (`gateway: ready`, `last pass: <old time>, ok`). The troubleshooting row for `helper-already-running` says 'Another helper is running' and only treats `pid: -1` as a stale lock, so an operator following it concludes the helper is up; the only tell is the age of the last-pass timestamp, which nothing compares. No test covers a live pid that is not a helper (the tests use the test's own pid or a dead one). Fix by proving the owner is a helper before honouring the lock (compare the pid's command, or record and compare a start time), and by having `status` treat a snapshot whose `pid` differs from the lock's or whose `at` is older than the backoff ceiling as 'not confirmed running'.

observations.summary: A fully posted item whose last part was never reported is acknowledged again on every pass, forever, once its item is gone
observations.recommendation: Scope: instance. lib/bridge-helper/outbound.js#acknowledge, the `unbound` branch: the entry is forgotten only when `entry.receipted >= entry.parts.length`. An entry with status `posted`, a stored leaseId and an unreported last part (the post landed, the part report did not: bridge unreachable, or the lease lapsed during the helper's backoff, which reaches 5 minutes against a 2 minute lease) is retried by the first loop of pass() on every poll. If the item is still waiting this heals on the next claim. If the item was meanwhile withdrawn, let go, or set aside, it is never handed over again, the stale lease answers 409 LEASE_LAPSED for good, pass() stays ok (no backoff), and the helper makes one doomed acknowledgement and writes one `outbound-ack-failed` line every pollSeconds until someone deletes the record. Before this commit the same state answered OUTBOUND_EXPIRED / OUTBOUND_BLOCKED and the helper forgot the entry. Nothing is posted twice and nothing is lost at the bridge; the cost is an unbounded log and a request per poll, which also undoes the basis on which the helper-log growth warning was accepted (it grows per relayed message and per failure only). No test reaches this state: test/bridge-helper-relay.test.js 'lets go of its record when the bridge has let the item go' loses only the acknowledgement, so every part is already receipted. Fix without any oracle: a lease answered LEASE_LAPSED, LEASE_NOT_FOUND or LEASE_NOT_YOURS can never become usable, so on `unbound` drop the dead leaseId from the saved entry (pass() only re-acknowledges entries that carry one); a re-claim sets a fresh lease in relay(). Add the test: last part posted, part report lost, item withdrawn or let go, two passes, exactly one `outbound-ack-failed`. docs/operator-bridge-helper.md 'One case leaves something behind ... It does no harm' should then cover this entry too. ACCEPT is available if the Architect prefers the noise to a helper change; it is the direct answer to 'can the helper strand an item because it is no longer told the item is gone'.

findings.summary: A post's delivery outcome in relay() is reconstructed from five signals across four sites, with no single classifier
findings.recommendation: Scope: class (every outcome of one createMessage attempt in lib/bridge-helper/outbound.js relay(); bounded to that function, its two helpers and discord-rest.js's `sent`). Why it broke: each ruling (Decision 23's 400, chat-closed, reply-target, and now bare 403/404 and unplaceable) was added as another guarded `if` rather than as a row of one outcome table. Conditions observed. Signals: (1) err.sent, set in discord-rest.js call() from the status range ('no' for 3xx/4xx and pre-connect causes, 'unknown' for 5xx/timeouts, and a synthetic 502/'unknown' for a 200 with no id); (2) err.status; (3) err.discordCode; (4) `opened` (whether THIS iteration wrote entry.since); (5) `unthreaded`, a mutable local flipped inside the inner catch and the only carrier of 'the one retry already happened'. Outcomes: posted; retried unthreaded; rejected-by-chat (forget, return held); uncertain (save status 'uncertain', report outcome-unverifiable, return held); chat closed x4 reasons (forget, throw Reported); unplaceable (report outcome-unverifiable, forget, return held); transient (throw); outcome-unknown (throw). Decided at: discord-rest.js call(); replyTargetMayBeMissing(); configurationReason(err, unthreaded); and four inline ifs at outbound.js:450-479 whose ORDER is load-bearing (400 before closed, closed before the 4xx range, a literal `status !== 429`) and which each repeat `notSent && opened`. Consequences already visible at HEAD: (a) `outcome-unverifiable` is produced at three sites with two different helper-side states - held as `uncertain` (lines 410, 459) and forgotten (line 477) - so the bridge's block code no longer says whether the helper holds anything; (b) line 478 returns outcome 'held' for an item the helper just forgot, while pass() derives its `held` count from state instead (the new test asserts held: 0 for it), so 'held' has two meanings; (c) replyTargetMayBeMissing re-tests `!CONFIGURATION_CODES[code]`, knowledge configurationReason owns, and retries on ANY 404 that carries a non-configuration code, where its JSDoc and ADR Decision 23 say a bare 404; (d) a definite refusal while an earlier attempt is in doubt (`!opened`) goes straight to `uncertain` for 400 but falls through to `transient` for 401/403/404/other 4xx, because both later branches are gated on `opened` and nothing states that pairing as intended. No invalid combination was found reachable (every path converges: the in-doubt case ends as `uncertain` once the nonce window passes), hence warning, not blocking. Remedy is a construction, not another branch: one pure function, e.g. classifyPost({status, sent, discordCode}, {opened, unthreaded, threaded}) returning one member of a closed outcome set (retry-unthreaded | rejected | uncertain | closed:<reason> | unplaceable | transient | unknown), with relay() switching on that result for the side effects (clear since / save / forget / report / return vs throw). The table test at test/bridge-helper-relay.test.js:680-688 then pins the whole matrix, including the `!opened` rows that today have no stated ruling.
